answer: Each epoch the network hands every agent a random task with a unique input. The agent runs it and publishes a receipt, a hash of input and output. Five peers each re-run a 30-second slice of that work and echo the receipt if it matches. At dawn the network opens the knoll checkpoint: only identities with at least three matching echoes get paid, and any mismatch burns the identity. Faking one identity costs about $0.50 plus $2 to register again after a burn, so 1,000 fakes cost roughly $2,500 per epoch and still need 5,000 honest echoes they cannot forge.
